sprint: Magic Publish — Sprint M9 (Launch Readiness). Per docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md: "Goal. Create a feature people talk about. Scope. Review animation quality, timing, transitions, delight, consistency, and branding. Output. Launch-ready Magic Publish." The last sprint of the Magic Publish plan — a review sprint, so the work was to audit what M1-M8 actually produced against the six product acceptance tests and then fix only what the audit genuinely found.
task: Audited rather than assumed, and measured rather than eyeballed — four findings, all four fixed. (1) BRAND-LINE INCONSISTENCY: the video's closing card said '✨ Created in VihuPlanet ✨' while the Magic Strip footer said 'Made in VihuPlanet' — two wordings on a feature that already deliberately shares FILM_BG/BRAND_FG so it "closes on one look rather than two". (2) CARD TYPEFACE NEITHER ON-BRAND NOR DETERMINISTIC: the card drew in `Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif`, none of which VihuStudio self-hosts; measured on this machine, wGeorgia === wSerif === wTimes === wBogus === 544.810546875 — a deliberately bogus family measures identically, proving universal fallback, so the one frame carrying the brand rendered in whatever face that machine happened to have. document.fonts.check('700 74px Georgia') returning true is misleading: it returns true for anything the system can RESOLVE, including via fallback. (3) A REAL SHIPPED BUG — THE MAGIC STRIP DREW IN A FALLBACK FONT: nunitoBefore was false on a fresh page and the same string measured 342.99 before vs 366 after document.fonts.load('700 40px Nunito'); nothing else on the page asks for Nunito (no font-family: Nunito anywhere in css/style.css or index.html), so every strip caption and its brand line were genuinely drawing in the fallback face. (4) CARD COMPOSITION: the companion was 340px = 31% of frame width with ~35% dead space above and below, and the glow at rgba(255,203,69,0.13) was barely perceptible, so the card read as flat brown-black rather than a warm sky. THE FIXES. MagicStrip becomes the single source of truth for both halves: it now exports BRAND_LINE ('✨ Created in VihuPlanet') and FONT_STACK ('"Nunito", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif'), and storyDestinations reads them through _magicBrandLine()/_magicFontStack() — defensive-optional in the same typeof X!=='undefined' shape as every other cross-module read in that file, with fallbacks that are the same literals MagicStrip declares. Georgia is gone; both halves now draw in self-hosted Nunito. For the font race, MagicStrip gains a memoised ensureFonts() that document.fonts.load()s Nunito at 600 and 700, kicked once in publishStudio.open() right beside the existing SlideRenderer.preloadFonts call — the precedent whose own comment already explains that _ensureCanvasFont's redraw-on-ready only helps the LIVE editor canvas and is useless for a one-shot Publish export — and AWAITED explicitly inside _magicClosingCard, so the one frame carrying the brand gets a guarantee rather than only a head start. Deliberately did NOT make MagicStrip.compose() or the STRIP destination's encodePage async: that would be a signature change to shipped M5 code, against "never refactor architecture without approval", and the head start plus the card's own await covers it. Composition: companion 340->520 (31%->48% of frame width), title 74->92, brand 40->48, gap 46->52, glow 0.13->0.24 with a 0.06 mid stop and its centre moved to H*0.44 so the companion sits inside the light, plus a 220-unit gold hairline rule between title and brand so the two read as separate beats rather than one stack of centred text. Block-height arithmetic was hand-verified to still balance (top gap ~545px vs bottom ~525px). CONFIRMED ALREADY CONSISTENT, needing no change: the stage labels are genuinely shared between the video and the Strip (GROUP_LABELS/BLANK_LABEL/FINISHED_LABEL). Verified 21/21 via a new magic_m9_verify suite across five sections, ordered so the decisive check runs before anything on the page has touched fonts: A confirms one BRAND_LINE, a Nunito-first FONT_STACK and an exported ensureFonts; B is the font proof — Nunito is genuinely COLD on a fresh page (false), rendering the closing card is itself what loads it, and a cold render and a warm render are BYTE-IDENTICAL, which is what distinguishes 'awaited correctly' from 'happened to be warm', plus ensureFonts being memoised; A4/A5 stub MagicStrip.BRAND_LINE and FONT_STACK and require the card's pixels to change, proving the card reads the shared constants rather than keeping a second copy; C stubs the companion portrait with a solid-magenta square and measures the drawn bounding box directly — 519x519 against an expected 520, contain-fit square, 48.1% of frame width, with the glow measurably warmer at the light centre than at a corner (delta 39); D composes a real strip and counts gold brand pixels in the footer's right half (685); E publishes end to end and reads EBML magic 1a45dfa3 off the blob's own first four bytes (1.67MB video/webm). ONE TEST-METHODOLOGY BUG, disclosed rather than glossed over and not an app bug: section E first queried '.publish-destination-format' grid-wide, but every destination card renders its own format list, so it picked Story Book's first format and published a PDF; scoped to the Magic card. Regression: magic_m1 32/32, magic_m2 33/33, magic_m3 32/32, magic_m4 41/41, magic_m5 43/43, magic_m6 35/35, magic_m7 38/38, magic_m8 47/47, reel 15/15, reel_backdrop 10/10, reel_pageturn 12/12, voice 16/16, voice_note 22/22, both goldenBuilds PASS. renderer/slideRenderer.js untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship.
